Attach a safety condition to a watcher

Source: R/guards.R
guard.Rd

Wraps the watcher's existing callback so it only fires when condition() returns TRUE. If the condition fails, the event is logged and the on_fail action is taken instead.

Usage

guard(
  id,
  condition,
  message = "Guard condition failed",
  on_fail = c("warn", "stop", "silent")
)

Arguments

id

Character. Watcher ID to protect.

condition

A zero-argument function that returns TRUE (safe to fire) or FALSE (hold back), or a one-sided formula ~ expr.

message

Character. Human-readable reason shown when the guard blocks the callback.

on_fail

One of "warn" (default), "stop", or "silent". What to do when the guard blocks.

Value

Invisibly TRUE.

Details

Multiple guards can be attached to the same watcher. They are evaluated in the order they were added, and all must pass for the callback to fire.

See also

throttle(), disk_ok(), mem_ok(), net_ok()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
id <- on_arrive("~/cbn_feeds/", action = function(event, path) {
  opennaijR::fetch("NGA", "inflation")
})

# Only fetch if disk is not critically full
guard(id,
      condition = ~ disk_ok(threshold = 0.90),
      message   = "Disk over 90 percent full - skipping fetch")

# Only fetch if available memory > 500 MB
guard(id,
      condition = ~ mem_ok(min_mb = 500),
      message   = "Low memory - pipeline paused")
} # }
